title: Wasps Recognize Faces, and a Close Cousin Can't
subject: northern paper wasp

scenes.text: Wasps can recognize faces. Their close cousin can't.
Northern paper wasps remember each other's facial markings and use them to settle who is queen without costly fights.
In a test, wasps in a T-shaped maze had to avoid an electrified floor by learning which image marked the safe arm.
They learned wasp faces faster and more accurately than any other image, even caterpillars, which are favorite prey.
A close but solitary relative did no better than chance at telling faces apart.
Only the wasps that live in groups needed faces. So only they learned them.
